name: por-ramp-rate
description: Full-assembly supply ramp-rate envelope check of design/netlist/temp_por_top.spice: four monotonic 0->VDD ramps (1 V/s, 10 V/s, 0.1 V/us, 1 V/us -- both ratified endpoints plus one decade inside each) run together in one transient, each checked for RESETn held low from 0 V through the ramp and then released once and only once, at or above VPOR-uparrow,min.
claim: spec/target-spec.md#por-ramp-rate -- "correct" = RESETn low from 0 V throughout the ramp, released once and only once, no early release, no glitch, no double pulse, at both ratified endpoints (1 V/s, 1 V/us) plus one decade inside each (10 V/s, 0.1 V/us), over the full PVT grid, on the real four-cell assembly (bias_core-driven IBIAS, nothing idealised). Deterministic corners only (design.ngspice sets sw_stat_mismatch=0); mismatch is #15's job. The 1 V/us branch is expected to intersect design/bias_core.md's already-owned starved-loop window (BIAS_OK false-valid while VREF is still parked, measured up to ~1.6 ms at the bias_core cell level) -- see that document and this testbench's stimulus header before treating a miss there as a new defect.

vddrel_1vs_v.description: spec/target-spec.md#por-ramp-rate slow limit (1 V/s), 'no early release': the rail voltage at the instant RESETn releases must be at or above VPOR-uparrow,min = 2.47 V, the ratified minimum release threshold. Releasing below that is an early release by the ratified spec regardless of what caused it. Ceiling is the rail itself (3.63 V + slack).

vddrel_10vs_v.description: one decade inside the slow limit (10 V/s), same no-early-release floor.

vddrel_100kvs_v.description: one decade inside the fast limit (0.1 V/us), same no-early-release floor. At this rate the ramp finishes in 30-36 us while the reset pulse runs for milliseconds, so release lands at the settled rail rather than near the threshold -- the floor is still the correct criterion, it is simply far from binding.

vddrel_1mvs_v.description: spec/target-spec.md#por-ramp-rate fast limit (1 V/us), same no-early-release floor as every other rate. Deliberately NOT relaxed for design/bias_core.md's already-owned starved-loop window: if that window makes this branch release below VPOR-uparrow,min, the ratified row is not met at its fast endpoint and this record must say so (CLAUDE.md: agents do not relax the ratified spec to make results pass). The record's own text, and design/bias_core.md, then carry it to #1 as a re-cost.

chatter_1vs_us.description: no double pulse at 1 V/s: first and last rising crossing of RESETn must coincide.

chatter_1mvs_us.description: no double pulse at 1 V/us, held to the SAME 1 ns bound as the slower rates. An earlier draft of this manifest widened it to +/-5 ms to accommodate the starved-loop window; that was wrong -- a genuine double pulse is separated by at least one reset-pulse width (>=1 ms ratified, 4.2-17.0 ms measured), so a +/-5 ms band would have passed exactly the failure the row forbids.

resetn_at_1v_1vs_mv.description: spec/target-spec.md#por-ramp-rate's 'RESETn low from 0 V throughout the ramp', probed at a 1 V rail. Each DUT's rail is rate*t by construction, so t = 1/rate samples exactly 1 V: 1 s at 1 V/s, 0.1 s at 10 V/s, 10 us at 0.1 V/us, 1 us at 1 V/us. Slow-ramp early release is the classic POR field failure this row exists to forbid.

resetn_at_2v_1vs_mv.description: same, at a 2 V rail -- still 0.47 V below VPOR-uparrow,min, so RESETn must still be low.

t_release_1vs_ms.description: liveness: RESETn must actually release inside the run at the slow limit. At 1 V/s the rail needs 2.47-2.73 s just to reach the threshold, so this bound is a 'the DUT is alive and the run is long enough' guard, not a timing claim -- the pulse-width claim is sim/por-brownout/'s t_pulse_regen_ms and sim/por-output-chain-pulse/'s.

unchecked_measurement_notes.vref_at_rel_1mvs_v: Recorded, deliberately NOT checked. bias_core's reference at the instant the fast-limit branch releases -- the direct read of whether design/bias_core.md's starved-loop window is still open at that moment. It is diagnostic context for whatever vddrel_1mvs_v/chatter_1mvs_us report, not a bound of its own.
unchecked_measurement_notes.biasok_at_rel_1mvs_v: Recorded, deliberately NOT checked, same reason: BIAS_OK's state at the fast-limit release instant distinguishes 'released on a settled reference' from 'released inside the false-valid window'.
